chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was revealed, it was among the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): "Greet Ali as Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Believers)." And it was among what God had affirmed upon them both on that day — O Zayd — the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to them both: "Arise and greet him as Amir al-Mu'minin." They said: "Is it from God or from His Messenger, O Messenger of God?" And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: "From God and from His Messenger."

Then God Mighty and Majestic revealed [16:91]: "And do not break the oaths after confirming them, while you have made God a surety over you; surely God knows what you do" — meaning by this the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to them both and their words: "Is it from God or from His Messenger?"
[16:92]: "And do not be like the one who unravels her yarn after spinning it strongly; you make your oaths a means of deceit between you so that the Imams would be more virtuous than your leaders."

He (the narrator) said: I said: "May I be your ransom — Imams?" He said: "Yes, by God, Imams." I said: "But we recite 'arbaa' (أَرْبَى)." He said: "What is 'arbaa'?" And he gestured with his hand and discarded it.

[16:92 cont.]: "Indeed, God tests you by it" — meaning by Ali (peace be upon him) — "and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that in which you differed. [16:93] And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation; but He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills; and you will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what you used to do."

[16:94]: "And do not make your oaths a means of deceit between you, lest a foot slip after its firmness" — meaning after the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali (peace be upon him) — "and you would taste evil for having turned away from the way of God" — meaning by it Ali (peace be upon him) — "and for you will be a great punishment."

key_terms.أَئِمَّة: Imams — the divinely appointed leaders of the Shia community
key_terms.أَزْكَى: More virtuous/pure — the Imam's recitation of the Quran, differing from standard text
key_terms.إِمْرَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin — Commander of the Believers, the title of Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilayah — divine guardianship and authority, specifically the legitimate leadership of the Imam
key_terms.يَبْلُوكُمُ: He tests you — a Quranic phrase the Imam interprets as referring to Ali (AS)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the revelation of Ali's authority as Amir al-Mu'minin?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recounts the momentous event of the revelation of Ali's wilayah (divinely appointed authority) and the command to acknowledge him as Amir al-Mu'minin. The Imam explains that Surah al-Nahl verses 91-94 were revealed precisely in response to two companions' hesitant question about whether this command came from God or the Prophet — with the Prophet affirming both — and provides an esoteric reading of these verses where 'Imams' replaces the standard Quranic text. The historical context here is the event of Ghadir Khumm and its aftermath, making this a pivotal Shia document connecting Quranic revelation to the explicit designation of the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Zayd Bin Al Jahm Al Hilaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the Wilayah of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> was Revealed, and it was from the words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>: ‘Greet upon Ali<sup>asws</sup> as Amir Al-Momineen (The Commander of the Believers)’. So it was from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup> had Affirmed upon them both during that day, O Zayd, the words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> to them both (Abu Bakr and Umar) were: ‘Arise you both and greet upon him<sup>asws</sup> as Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>’. So they said, ‘Is it from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> or from His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’

So Rasool-Allahsaww said to them: ‘(It is) from Allahazwj and Hisazwj Rasoolsaww’. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Revealed [16:91] and do not break the oaths after affirming them, and you have indeed made Allah a surety for you; surely Allah Knows what you are doing, Meaning by it the words of Rasool-Allahsaww to the two of them, and their words, ‘It is from Allahazwj or from Hisazwj Rasoolsaww?’

[16:92] And be not like her who unravels her yarn, disintegrating it into pieces after having spun it strongly. You make your oaths to be means of deceit between you so that the Imams would happen to be more virtuous than your own leaders’. (Note – The words in red are different in the current Version of the Holy Quran).

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Imams<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Imams<sup>asws</sup>’. I said, ‘But we are reciting ‘More beneficial’ (أَرْبى)!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is (this word) ‘أَرْبى’?’

And heasws gestured by hisasws hand, so heasws discarded them (indicatively) [16:92] But rather, Allah is Testing you by this, Meaning by Aliasws and He will Clarify to you on the Day of Judgement that which you were differing in [16:93] And had Allah so Desired it He would Make you a single nation, but He Lets err whomsoever He Desires to and Guides whomsoever He Desires to; and you will be Questioned about what you had been doing [16:94] And do not make your oaths a means of deceit between you, lest a foot should slip after its stability Meaning after the words of Rasool-Allahsaww regarding Aliasws and you would taste evil because you turned away from Allah's Way Meaning by it ‘Aliasws’, and a grievous Punishment would be for you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Mansur ibn Yunus from Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali who has said that heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say the following.

“When Wilaya of (the declaration that ) Ali ibn abu Talib has (Divine Authority over the people) descended and it was in the words of the Messenger of Allah they all greeted and congratulated Ali (a.s.) as the commander of the believers. Of the matters that Allah had stressed up on the two of them on that day, O Zayd was what came through the words of the Messenger of Allah for the two of them. “The two of you stand up and congratulate him (Ali ) as the commander of the believers. The two of them asked, “Is it from Allah or from the Messenger of Allah, O the Messenger of Allah ?” The Messenger of Allah then said to the two of them, “It is from Allah and from His Messenger.”

Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, then sent the following. “. . (He commands people) to keep their established covenants with God not to disregard their firm oaths; they have already appointed God as their Guarantor. God certainly knows what you do.” [16:91] The Imam (a.s.) said , “It refers to the words of the Messenger of Allah to the two of them and thier words to the the Messenger of Allah saying, “Is it from Allah or from the Messenger of Allah, O the Messenger of Allah ?”

The point to note in this matter in the following words of Allah is Imams. “Do not be like the lady behind the spinning wheel who has broken the yarn by pulling it with unnecessary force. You must not consider your oaths as means of deceit to benefit one party and incur loss upon the other. . .” [16:92], just because they are the Imams who possess highier spiritual standard.”

The narrator has said that he then asked the Imam (a.s.), ‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, is the word ’A’imma (Imams)? However, we read it Arba’? The Imam (a.s.) then said, “What Arba’ is it that you mention? He made a gesture with his hand as an indication of throwing away something and said,

“Allah tests you through him (Ali (a.s.) “. . He will make clear to you who was right and who was wrong on the Day of Judgment. [16:92] Had God wanted, He would have made you one single nation but He guides or causes to go astray whomever He wants. You will certainly be questioned about what you have done. [16:93]

Do not consider your oaths as a means of deceit lest you damage the firmness of your faith, (after what you have heard from the Messenger of Allah about Ali (a.s.) ) suffer from evil by creating obstacles in the way that leads to God, (a reference to Ali (a.s.) ) and incur a great torment upon yourselves [16:94].”
